newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Sept 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Sept 25.

text.p: 100,000 STG A HOUSE AS PRICES TAKE OFF

The average price of a London property now exceeds 100,000 stg, according to official figures from the Land Registry which show an increase in house prices in the capital of 5.5 percent in the first sixth months of the year.
CLARKE CONFIDENT ON IMF GOLD SALES PLAN

Chancellor Kenneth Clarke is hopeful that his plan to assist some of the world's most debt-ridden countries by selling part of the IMF's gold reserves, is about to be agreed following two years of disputes. The plan proposes that the IMF sells a fraction of its $40 billion gold reserves and then uses the interest from the sale to alleviate the debts of countries like Uganda and Mozambique.
PRU LAUNCHES "PHONE BANKING WITH A FACE'

The Prudential is today launching its own bank, which will combine phone banking with 6,300 sales agents who will visit potential customers' homes. The man behind the new service is Mike Harris, who launched Midland's First Direct telephone banking service in 1989.
MARKETS STILL SEEK U.S. RATE RISE

Money markets are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise U.S. interest rates at the next meeting of its Open Market Committee, despite causing shocks all round by not making any move yesterday.
BA WARNS U.S. LINK WILL FAIL IF HEATHROW SLOTS ARE LOST

British Airways has warned the government that it will call off its proposed alliance with American Airlines if a condition of avoiding referral to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission is giving up Heathrow slots to competitors.
CHINA SETS SUPERHIGHWAY WHEELS IN MOTION

China is to spend eight billion stg on setting up a national information superhighway over the next five years, and has invited outside companies, but currently only those in Hong Kong, to contribute capital and expertise to the project.
